questions.text: Which of the following best describes the purpose of a quality indicator?

options.a: To measure staff performance for annual appraisals
options.b: To track and evaluate the quality of care delivered against defined standards
options.c: To report incidents to external regulatory agencies
options.d: To benchmark physician salaries against national averages

questions.explanation: Quality indicators are measurable elements used to monitor and evaluate the quality of patient care and organizational performance against established standards.

questions.text: Peer review in a healthcare quality context primarily serves to:

options.b: Evaluate clinical performance and identify opportunities for improvement
options.c: Replace the role of the quality department in monitoring outcomes

questions.explanation: Peer review is a formal process where clinicians evaluate each other's practice to identify deviations from accepted standards and opportunities for quality improvement.

questions.text: A hospital's quality council is reviewing a department that consistently exceeds its infection rate benchmark. The FIRST step in the quality review process should be:

options.b: Collect and analyze data to understand the root cause of the variance
options.c: Report the department to state health authorities
options.d: Benchmark against a lower-performing hospital to appear favorable

questions.explanation: The first step in quality review is data-driven analysis to understand why performance deviates from the benchmark before implementing any interventions or actions.

questions.text: Which of the following is an example of a structural measure of quality?

options.b: Percentage of patients who received discharge instructions
options.c: Number of board-certified physicians on staff

questions.explanation: Structural measures assess the attributes of the care setting — such as facilities, personnel qualifications, and organizational characteristics. Board certification is a structural measure. Process and outcome measures assess what is done and what results.

questions.text: In a quality management framework, accountability means:

options.a: Only senior leadership is responsible for quality outcomes
options.b: Each role in the organization has defined quality responsibilities and is answerable for results
options.c: Quality is the sole responsibility of the quality department
options.d: Accountability is only applied when a regulatory body demands it

questions.explanation: True quality accountability is distributed throughout the organization. Each department, team, and individual has defined responsibilities for quality and is expected to report on and own their performance.
